exposure: delivery without perineum and/or fetal head support
outcome: maternal birth trauma (including first-degree tear, obstetric anal sphincter injuries (OASIs), and cervical laceration)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 424 mothers who had singleton vaginal deliveries at University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospital.
finding: The study found that 47.4% of mothers experienced birth trauma after vaginal delivery, with primiparity, gestational age >= 39 weeks, heavier birth weight, bigger head circumference, operative vaginal delivery, and lack of perineum/fetal head support significantly associated with its occurrence.
mod_finding: Operative vaginal delivery was significantly associated with an increased risk of maternal birth trauma.
